Find the arc length of the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ from $t=0$ to $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Arc Length of a Vector-Valued Function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14052793/assets/e6de928031610e2aaf55e3dd753449f766e7dc028a6618087e7489224a73ea7d.png)

Find the arc length of the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$
from  $t=0$ to $t=2.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}} \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $t\ge 0$ for $t\in [0,2].$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{2}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{2}}{2})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
